title: docs-schema.yaml
description:
`docs-schema.yaml`: the documentation fields your company keeps about its interfaces, destinations and resources, beyond what Ductus asks for (a BAA reference, a change ticket, a runbook link, the analyst). Values go in `custom:` beside each one; `ductus validate` checks them, and the web UI shows and filters by them. The engine itself ignores them.

The file sits at the top of the project and is optional: without it there are no fields.

fields.description: The fields, by the key `custom:` uses, in the order the web UI shows them. Keys are your choice, except names Ductus uses beside `custom` (`name`, `owner`, `vendor`, …). Default: none. Example: `fields: { baa_signed: { type: enum, values: ["yes", "no"], required: true } }`.
fields.markdownDescription: The fields, by the key `custom:` uses, in the order the web UI shows them. Keys are your choice, except names Ductus uses beside `custom` (`name`, `owner`, `vendor`, …). Default: none. Example: `fields: { baa_signed: { type: enum, values: ["yes", "no"], required: true } }`.

type.description:
What the value is:

- `text`: any text (quote numbers and yes/no, or YAML reads them as such).
- `enum`: one of `values`.
- `date`: a date, written `2026-10-30`.
- `url`: an `http(s)://` address, shown as a link.
- `person`: who, as text: best an email address.
- `list`: several texts (each one of `values`, if given).

Required. Example: `type: enum`.
type.markdownDescription:
What the value is:

- `text`: any text (quote numbers and yes/no, or YAML reads them as such).
- `enum`: one of `values`.
- `date`: a date, written `2026-10-30`.
- `url`: an `http(s)://` address, shown as a link.
- `person`: who, as text: best an email address.
- `list`: several texts (each one of `values`, if given).

Required. Example: `type: enum`.

values.description: The values an `enum` may take (and each item of a `list`, if given), matched exactly, case included. Quote ones YAML would read otherwise (`"yes"`, `"no"`). Default: none. Example: `values: ["yes", "no", n/a]`.
values.markdownDescription: The values an `enum` may take (and each item of a `list`, if given), matched exactly, case included. Quote ones YAML would read otherwise (`"yes"`, `"no"`). Default: none. Example: `values: ["yes", "no", n/a]`.

required.description: Every interface (destination, resource) the field applies to must have a value: `ductus validate` reports each one missing. The engine starts anyway. Default: `false`. Example: `required: true`.
required.markdownDescription: Every interface (destination, resource) the field applies to must have a value: `ductus validate` reports each one missing. The engine starts anyway. Default: `false`. Example: `required: true`.

applies_to.description: Where the field may be given: `interface`, `destination` and/or `resource` (a resources.yaml entry). Default: `[interface]`. Example: `applies_to: [interface, resource]`.
applies_to.markdownDescription: Where the field may be given: `interface`, `destination` and/or `resource` (a resources.yaml entry). Default: `[interface]`. Example: `applies_to: [interface, resource]`.

label.description: The name the web UI shows instead of the key. Default: the key. Example: `label: BAA signed`.
label.markdownDescription: The name the web UI shows instead of the key. Default: the key. Example: `label: BAA signed`.

help.description: A hint shown under the field in the web UI: what it's for, or where to find the value. Default: none. Example: `help: Business associate agreement, from the contracts office`.
help.markdownDescription: A hint shown under the field in the web UI: what it's for, or where to find the value. Default: none. Example: `help: Business associate agreement, from the contracts office`.
